lines.text: Can a 160 dollar Honda clone keep up with the real 600 dollar Honda?
The clone even copies Honda's red paint and its label claims way more horsepower.
But a sticker is just a sticker so he runs both on generators for 48 hours to find the truth.
On the vibration tester the clone shakes so hard the meter can't even read it.
Because a one cylinder engine fires on just one side so it needs a well balanced crankshaft to stay smooth.
beats: ai:cutaway of a single cylinder small gas engine with the piston firing
ai:a steel crankshaft with heavy counterweights spinning fast in a dark workshop

lines.text: Then it burns so much oil he tops it up twice in a day like a leaky boat.
beats: ai:an old leaky wooden rowboat slowly filling with water on a lake

lines.text: That oil slips past the piston rings and burns which is why its spark plug is caked in carbon.
beats: ai:macro of motor oil slipping past a piston ring inside an engine cylinder

lines.text: And on the pull test the clone makes 200 pounds while the real Honda makes 239.
But the twist is the cheap Harbor Freight Predator which pulls 233.
That's within three percent of the Honda and it even wins the kart race with the fastest average time.
So which one would you buy?

title: Which $150 Engine Can Keep Up With a $600 Honda? 🤔 (@ProjectFarm/YT)
description: Project Farm ran a Honda, a Honda clone, a Predator and a Briggs for 48 hours and pulled a trailer with each. The fake's sticker lies, and the cheap surprise is the Predator.
